1.web: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.
1.asv: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, Mine ear hath heard and understood it.

2.web: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.
2.asv: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.

3.web: “Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.
3.asv: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason with God.

4.web: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.
4.asv: But ye are forgers of lies; Ye are all physicians of no value.

5.web: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
5.asv: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! And it would be your wisdom.

6.web: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.
6.asv: Hear now my reasoning, And hearken to the pleadings of my lips.

7.web: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?
7.asv: Will ye speak unrighteously for God, And talk deceitfully for him?

8.web: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?
8.asv: Will ye show partiality to him? Will ye contend for God?

9.web: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?
9.asv: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceiveth a man, will ye deceive him?

10.web: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.
10.asv: He will surely reprove you, If ye do secretly show partiality.

11.web: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall on you?
11.asv: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall upon you?

12.web: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.
12.asv: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defences are defences of clay.

13.web: “Be silent, leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.
13.asv: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak; And let come on me what will.

14.web: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
14.asv: Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hand?

15.web: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.
15.asv: Behold, he will slay me; I have no hope: Nevertheless I will maintain my ways before him.

16.web: This also shall be my salvation, that a godless man shall not come before him.
16.asv: This also shall be my salvation, That a godless man shall not come before him.

17.web: Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.
17.asv: Hear diligently my speech, And let my declaration be in your ears.

18.web: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.
18.asv: Behold now, I have set my cause in order; I know that I am righteous.

19.web: Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.
19.asv: Who is he that will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the ghost.

20.web: “Only don’t do two things to me; then I will not hide myself from your face:
20.asv: Only do not two things unto me; Then will I not hide myself from thy face:

21.web: withdraw your hand far from me; and don’t let your terror make me afraid.
21.asv: Withdraw thy hand far from me; And let not thy terror make me afraid.

22.web: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
22.asv: Then call thou, and I will answer; Or let me speak, and answer thou me.

23.web: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.
23.asv: How many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to know my transgression and my sin.

24.web: Why hide you your face, and hold me for your enemy?
24.asv: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And holdest me for thine enemy?

25.web: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
25.asv: Wilt thou harass a driven leaf? And wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?

26.web: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:
26.asv: For thou writest bitter things against me, And makest me to inherit the iniquities of my youth:

27.web: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,
27.asv: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, And markest all my paths; Thou settest a bound to the soles of my feet:

28.web: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
28.asv: Though I am like a rotten thing that consumeth, Like a garment that is moth-eaten.
